question: Manoj bought two T.V. for Rs. 2,280, He sold one at a loss of 20 percent and other at a profit of 10 percent. If each TV was sold for the same price, then what is the cost price of the T.V which was sold at loss?
solution: **Given:** Manoj bought two TVs for Rs. 2,280. One TV was sold at a loss of 20% and the other at a profit of 10%. Calculation: CP₁ = Cost price of the first TV (the one sold at a loss). CP₂ = Cost price of the second TV (the one sold at a profit). We know from the given conditions that: CP₁ + CP₂ = Rs. 2,280 (since Manoj bought two TVs for this amount). Each TV was sold for the same price, which means: The price at which the first TV was sold (with a loss of 20%) equals the price at which the second TV was sold (with a profit of 10%). So, CP₁ - 20% of CP₁ = CP₂ + 10% of CP₂. Simplifying that, we get 0.8 × CP₁ = 1.1 × CP₂. 0.8 × CP₁ = 1.1 × (2,280 - CP₁) Solving this gives: 0.8 × CP₁ = 2,508 - 1.1 × CP₁ 1.9 × CP₁ = 2,508 CP₁ = Rs. 1,320 **So, the cost price of the TV which was sold at a loss is Rs. 1,320.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 1st article at loss = 20% = 1/5 2nd article at profit = 10% = 1/10 CP SP 1st 5 4 2nd 10 11 But both articles sold at the same SP. CP SP 1st 5 × 11= 55 4 × 11= 44 2nd 10 × 4 = 40 11 × 4 = 44 Total 95 88 Now, 95 unit = 2280 (Manoj bought two TVs for this amount) ⇒ 55 unit = 2280/95 × 55 = Rs. 1320 **∴ The cost price of the TV which was sold at a loss is Rs. 1,320.** 8c:T1c6d,
